📰 General

Ramaswamy Defends Campaign Ad Featuring Amy Acton’s Estranged Mother •

Republican presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy defended his campaign’s recent advertisement which depicts Amy Acton’s estranged mother. The ad, shown in northeast Ohio, sparked controversy due to its use of a personal and potentially sensitive image of Acton’s family. Ramaswamy stated the advertisement was intended to highlight Acton’s family history and background. The campaign has faced criticism for the ad’s tactics during the Ohio governor race.

🌍 World

Philippines Investigates Thomas Markle Over Alleged Child Sexual Abuse Images •

Philippine authorities are conducting an investigation into Thomas Markle following allegations that he possessed child sexual abuse images. The investigation was initiated by a complaint filed with the Philippine National Police, according to a justice undersecretary. The complaint alleges Mr. Markle had access to and potentially distributed the images. Authorities are currently seeking to verify the claims and determine if there is sufficient evidence to pursue further action.

🦅 US

Meghan’s Estranged Father Denies Child Porn Allegations as ‘Sick Lies’ •

Thomas Markle Sr., Meghan Markle’s estranged father, vehemently denies accusations that his son, Thomas Jr., claimed he possessed child sex images. He expressed shock and hurt regarding the allegations, stating they are “sick lies.” Markle Sr. has not provided any evidence to support his denials, according to sources. The claims originated from Thomas Jr., who made the accusations to the Daily Mail. Legal experts suggest the accusations are likely related to a previous dispute between the two men.

💰 Business

Mitsubishi Power Announces Major Expansion, Creating 220 Jobs in Georgia •

Mitsubishi Power Americas is investing $490 million in Chatham County, Georgia, to significantly expand its manufacturing operations. The company intends to create over 220 new jobs at the facility, representing nearly double its current footprint. This expansion will focus on increasing production capacity and strengthening the company’s presence in the region. Georgia Governor Brian Kemp and Chatham County Commissioners celebrated the investment, highlighting its positive impact on the local economy.

💻 Technology

Arkane Studios Faces Closure If “Blade” Fails to Secure a Buyer •

Arkane Lyon is nearing completion of its upcoming title, “Blade,” but the studio faces imminent closure if a buyer is not found within the next few weeks. A report in Le Monde indicates that the developers are actively seeking investment to avoid shuttering the studio. The situation stems from a lack of a definitive buyer, creating a critical deadline for the French studio. The future of Arkane Lyon’s operations hinges on securing additional funding to continue development.

🎭 Entertainment

Jane Wiseman Exits Paramount+ as HBO Max Merger Takes Effect •

Jane Wiseman, head of originals for Paramount+, is leaving the streaming service following the planned merger with HBO Max. This departure is being announced by Casey Bloys, who is now co-CEO and chief content officer for Skydance Direct-to-Consumer. The integration of the two platforms is reshaping content strategy and leadership roles within the combined entity. Details regarding Wiseman’s future plans are currently unavailable, but the shift signals a significant change in Paramount+'s direction.

🏅 Sports

Bears Win Over Patriots, But Cole Kmet Suffers Apparent Season-Ending Injury •

The Chicago Bears secured a 30-24 win against the New England Patriots on Sunday. During the fourth quarter, tight end Cole Kmet sustained a knee injury and was subsequently removed from the game via a stretcher. Initial reports indicate Kmet suffered a significant knee injury, prompting immediate medical attention. The extent of the injury is currently under evaluation, and the team has not yet provided a definitive timeline for his return.

🔬 Science

Ancient DNA Reveals Extensive Migration Patterns Across Ice Age Europe •

Recent genetic analysis of Paleolithic remains from across Europe has demonstrated a far greater level of interconnectedness among Gravettian people than previously understood. Researchers, led by the University of Vienna, examined DNA from numerous individuals dating back over 30,000 years. The study identified significant genetic links between populations in eastern and western Europe, suggesting a more complex and widespread cultural exchange. This discovery challenges previous assumptions about population isolation during the Ice Age and highlights the fluidity of ancient human movements.

🩺 Health

E. coli Cases Linked to Bengtson’s Pumpkin Farm in Will County •

Five individuals have been confirmed with E. coli infections potentially linked to visits to Bengtson’s Pumpkin Farm near Homer Glen, Illinois. The Will County Health Department is currently investigating the source of the contamination. Preliminary findings suggest a connection between the illnesses and the farm’s activities. Authorities are advising visitors to avoid the farm until the investigation is complete and potential risks are identified. The Health Department is working to determine the specific source of the bacteria.
